Kalnyk Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kalnyk, Ukraine

Not demolished. Presumably established in the 19th century, this cemetery existed by 1815 per epigraphic data, appearing on an 1865 cadastral map before later expansion; its latest surviving tombstone dates to 1927. Jews are believed to have arrived in the 18th century; population reached 212 by 1880, declining to 163 by 1921 (Czechoslovak period). Hungarian forces arrived March 1939, persecuting Jews and forcing them from their occupations; by 1941, area Jews were drafted into forced labor battalions, with others sent to the Eastern Front where most perished. A few families without Hungarian citizenship were expelled to Kamianets-Podilskyi and murdered; remaining Kalnyk Jews were deported to Auschwitz in late May 1944. No Jews live in the town today.
